nations.name: Puyallup Tribe of Indians
nations.lands: Shores of southern Puget Sound and the Puyallup River, Tacoma area, Washington

facts.text: One of the most urban tribes in the United States, the Puyallup still fish, hunt and travel the waters of the Puyallup River.
The Tribe gives its name as puyaləpabš, meaning people at the bend at the bottom of the river.

nations.name: Timbisha Shoshone Tribe
nations.lands: Death Valley and surrounding areas of California and Nevada

facts.text: Today the federally recognized Timbisha Shoshone Tribe works to keep its language, traditions and sovereignty strong.

source.title: Timbisha Shoshone Tribe - California and Nevada

facts.text: The Timbisha, part of the larger Western Shoshone people, have lived in Death Valley and its surrounding areas for thousands of years, and their village sits inside Death Valley National Park.

source.title: Timbisha Shoshone Tribe - California and Nevada

nations.name: Cahuilla Band of Indians
nations.lands: Anza area, Riverside County, Southern California

facts.text: The Band describes itself as a sovereign nation that carries its culture forward through strong governance.
Cahuilla traditional territory spans a large area of what are now Riverside and San Diego counties.

pronounce.text: kuh-WEE-eh (written on the Band's site as kəˊwi:e)
pronounce.publisher: Cahuilla Band of Indians, on its own site

nations.name: Washoe Tribe of Nevada and California
nations.lands: Lake Tahoe region and nearby valleys of western Nevada and eastern California

facts.text: Washoe teachers hold language classes for adults and youth four days a week, and immersion classes reach children in the tribe's Head Start.

source.title: Where Wašiw is Spoken: The Washoe Tribe is Passing Its Unique Language On and Up
source.publisher: Smithsonian National Museum of the American Indian (American Indian magazine)

facts.text: The name Tahoe is thought to come from Da ow ga, the Washoe word for lake.

source.title: Discover History
source.publisher: USDA Forest Service, Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit

nations.name: Cachil DeHe Band of Wintun Indians of the Colusa Indian Community
nations.lands: Colusa Rancheria near Colusa, California

facts.text: In 2004, the Colusa Indian Community Council published its first Cachil DeHe language book, a collaboration between Tribal Elders and University of California, Berkeley linguists.
In a January 2023 report, the Colusa Indian Community Council said its Housing Energy Connection Project extended the Tribe’s electric distribution to 33 households.

source.title: Housing Energy Connection Project Final Technical Report
source.publisher: Colusa Indian Community Council via U.S. Department of Energy

nations.name: Viejas Band of Kumeyaay Indians
nations.lands: Viejas Reservation in the mountains east of San Diego, California; the wider Kumeyaay homeland reaches into Baja California, Mexico

facts.text: Viejas extends its community work beyond San Diego to Kumeyaay relatives in Baja California, Mexico.
Viejas government rests on participatory democracy, with tribal officials elected by the general council to four-year terms.

nations.name: Santa Ynez Band of Chumash Indians
nations.lands: Santa Ynez Valley, Santa Barbara County, California

facts.text: The Tribe's Culture Department founded its language program in 2008, and the Tribe has unveiled a Samala-English Dictionary.

source.title: Culture
source.publisher: Santa Ynez Band of Chumash Indians

facts.text: Established on December 27, 1901, the Santa Ynez Reservation began with 99 acres and has grown to more than 1,500 acres.

source.title: The Santa Ynez Reservation
source.publisher: Santa Ynez Band of Chumash Indians

nations.name: Cahto Tribe of the Laytonville Rancheria
nations.lands: Laytonville Rancheria in Mendocino County, northern California

facts.text: The Tribe’s wetland plan records an April 27, 2001 water quality ordinance prohibiting pollutant discharge into waters within the Laytonville Rancheria.

source.title: Tribal Wetland Program Plan for the Cahto Tribe of the Laytonville Rancheria
source.publisher: Cahto Environmental Protection Department via U.S. EPA

facts.text: In its 2011 to 2015 wetland plan, the Tribe set a goal to restore impaired wetlands and maintain healthy wetlands within the Laytonville Rancheria.

source.title: Tribal Wetland Program Plan for the Cahto Tribe of the Laytonville Rancheria
source.publisher: Cahto Environmental Protection Department via U.S. EPA

nations.name: Confederated Tribes of Grand Ronde
nations.lands: Grand Ronde, Yamhill County, northwestern Oregon; ancestral ties across western Oregon, northern California and southwest Washington

facts.text: A nine-member Tribal Council, elected by voting members, governs about 5,400 enrolled members of a confederation of over 30 tribes and bands.
Once at risk of disappearing, Chinuk Wawa is growing again and is actively taught and used in Grand Ronde cultural education.

source.title: Chinuk Wawa Language | Confederated Tribes of Grand Ronde

nations.name: Burns Paiute Tribe
nations.lands: Near Burns in Harney County, Oregon

facts.text: On October 13, 1972, Congress established the Burns Paiute Reservation in trust for the Burns Indian Colony.
The Tribe recounts that Wadatika children kept speaking Paiute outside school after a small Tribal school opened in the 1920s.

nations.name: Nimiipuu
nations.lands: North-central Idaho, with homelands across present-day Idaho, Washington, Oregon and Montana

facts.text: Nimipuutímt, the Nez Perce language, is a core part of Nimiipuu culture.
Headquartered in Lapwai, Idaho, the Nez Perce Reservation spans about 770,000 acres.

nations.name: Berry Creek Rancheria of Tyme Maidu Indians of California
also: Berry Creek Rancheria of Maidu Indians of California
nations.lands: Oroville and the Tyme Maidu homelands in present-day Butte County, California

facts.text: Its education page links Tribal members to education-support materials, college programs and Native American scholarship resources.

source.title: Education Support | Berry Creek Rancheria
source.publisher: Berry Creek Rancheria of Tyme Maidu Indians of California

facts.text: The Tribe's account places Tyme Maidu homelands in what is now Butte County, with a relationship extending since time immemorial.

source.title: Our Story | Berry Creek Rancheria
source.publisher: Berry Creek Rancheria of Tyme Maidu Indians of California

nations.name: Cedarville Rancheria
nations.lands: Surprise Valley, Modoc County, northeastern California

facts.text: The Social Services Program states a mission of supporting Tribal members’ self-sufficiency and family stability.
In the constitutional text NARF received in 2003, the Community Council elects an executive committee.

source.title: Constitution and Bylaws of the Cedarville Rancheria
source.publisher: Cedarville Rancheria; hosted by NARF National Indian Law Library

nations.name: Bishop Paiute Tribe
nations.lands: Bishop, California, at the eastern Sierra Nevada

facts.text: The Education Center page describes goals for tutoring, college and career guidance, and support for students and parents.
In its July 7, 2026 broadband meeting update, the Tribe reported trenching progress and planning for home equipment installations.

nations.name: Karuk Tribe
nations.lands: Klamath River country of northern California, with tribal offices in Happy Camp

facts.text: The Karuk Language Program teaches all ages through community classes, school partnerships and immersion, linking learners with fluent speakers.
The Karuk People's Center in Happy Camp opened in September 2002 and holds a museum, library, basketweaving classroom and the language program office.

nations.name: Hoopa Valley Tribe
nations.lands: Hoopa Valley along the Trinity River, Humboldt County, northern California

facts.text: The Hoopa Valley Tribe runs its own Fisheries Department, which counts the harvest and spawning returns of salmon, steelhead, sturgeon and lamprey.
Tribal fisheries crews made major progress restoring the lower reaches of Supply Creek and Mill Creek between 2015 and 2018.

nations.name: Campo Band of Kumeyaay Indians
nations.lands: Laguna Mountains, southeastern San Diego County, California

facts.text: The agency reports that the Campo Band voted to end commercial grazing on Tribal lands effective January 1, 1995.
The agency’s account dates structures installed to control erosion in the Diebold Creek wetlands restoration project to 1992.

nations.name: Tolowa Dee-ni' Nation
nations.lands: Smith River and the coast of Del Norte County, far northern California

facts.text: The Tolowa Dee-ni' Nation was restored in 1983 through a court case, and its restored government extended citizenship to all Taa-laa-wa Dee-ni'.
Tolowa Dee-ni' language work goes back to a language program formed in 1969, and the Nation calls revitalization vital to Tolowa identity.

nations.name: Big Valley Band of Pomo Indians
nations.lands: Clear Lake area, Lake County, California

facts.text: Its history page reports adoption of a Master Land Use Plan in 1999, with a mission linking development, environmental protection and teaching Pomo culture.

source.title: About Us
source.publisher: Big Valley Band of Pomo Indians

facts.text: Big Valley’s monitoring page says it began Clear Lake cyanobacteria and cyanotoxin monitoring with Elem Indian Colony in 2014.

source.title: Clear Lake Cyanobacteria and Cyanotoxins Monitoring Program
source.publisher: Big Valley Band of Pomo Indians

nations.name: Bridgeport Indian Colony
nations.lands: Near Bridgeport in Mono County, California

facts.text: In 2010 testimony to Congress, the Colony’s chairman said its tribal government organized under the Indian Reorganization Act in 1976.

source.title: Bridgeport Indian Colony Prepared Testimony, July 28, 2010, p. 55
source.publisher: Bridgeport Indian Colony testimony, published by the U.S. House Committee on Natural Resources

facts.text: A law approved on October 18, 1974 declared the United States’ interest in specified Mono County land held in trust for Bridgeport Indian Colony.

nations.name: Makah Tribe
nations.lands: Neah Bay and Cape Flattery, at the northwest tip of Washington's Olympic Peninsula

facts.text: The name Makah came from neighboring tribes and means people generous with food.
The Makah Reservation at Neah Bay sits on the northwest tip of the continental United States.

nations.name: Tuolumne Band of Me-Wuk Indians
nations.lands: Sierra Nevada foothills, Tuolumne County, California

facts.text: In January 2005 the Tribe opened the Tuolumne Me-Wuk Indian Health Center.

source.title: History - The Tuolumne Band of Me-Wuk Indians

facts.text: Tuolumne Rancheria began in 1910 with 289.52 acres; today the Tribe holds more than 1,700 acres of fee and trust land.

source.title: History - The Tuolumne Band of Me-Wuk Indians

nations.name: Swinomish Indian Tribal Community
nations.lands: Swinomish Reservation near La Conner, Skagit County, Washington

facts.text: The Swinomish Tribe monitors air quality in partnership with the EPA, with two major oil refineries right next to its reservation.
Swinomish monitors record real-time data on particulates, ozone and nitrogen dioxide, plus weather such as wind, temperature, humidity and precipitation.

nations.name: Rapa Nui
nations.lands: Rapa Nui (Easter Island), in the south-eastern Pacific, Chile

facts.text: Tapati Rapa Nui, the island's main cultural festival, filled two weeks of February 2026 with ancestral competitions, arts and celebrations of Rapa Nui identity, language and traditions.

source.title: Ministra de las Culturas participa en inauguración de la Tapati Rapanui y desarrolla agenda de trabajo en la isla
source.publisher: Ministerio de las Culturas, las Artes y el Patrimonio (Chile)

facts.text: In 2017 Chile handed administration of Rapa Nui National Park to the Rapa Nui people, through the Ma'u Henua indigenous community, for 50 renewable years.

source.title: Presidenta Bachelet entrega administración del Parque Nacional Rapa Nui a la comunidad de Isla de Pascua
source.publisher: Ministerio del Interior y Seguridad Pública, Gobierno de Chile

nations.name: Aṉangu
nations.lands: Central Australia, including Uluṟu-Kata Tjuṯa in the Northern Territory and the APY Lands of South Australia

facts.text: The park's board of management has 12 people, including eight Aboriginal members nominated by Traditional Owners.

source.title: Joint management | Uluṟu-Kata Tjuṯa National Park | Parks Australia

facts.text: Uluṟu-Kata Tjuṯa National Park was handed back to its Aṉangu Traditional Owners in 1985 and is jointly managed today.

source.title: Joint management | Uluṟu-Kata Tjuṯa National Park | Parks Australia

nations.name: Kosraeans
nations.lands: Kosrae, an island state in the east of the Federated States of Micronesia, with the municipalities of Lelu, Malem, Tafunsak and Utwe

facts.text: Kosrae State has its own constitutional government, with a legislature elected by voters in the districts of Lelu, Malem, Tafunsak and Utwe.

source.title: Kosrae
source.publisher: Legal Information System of the Federated States of Micronesia

facts.text: In 2017 Kosraean elders proposed protecting Kosrae's mountain range, seen as the figure Mahkontowe, now the Mahkontowe Conservation Area under Kosrae State law.

nations.name: Moriori
nations.lands: Rēkohu and Rangihaute (the Chatham and Pitt Islands), Aotearoa New Zealand

facts.text: Moriori are the Indigenous people of Rēkohu and Rangihaute, the Chatham Islands, and are represented by the Hokotehi Moriori Trust.
The Hokotehi Moriori Trust takes part in key parts of the Rēkohu economy, such as fishing, farming and tourism.

nations.name: Gadigal
nations.lands: The southern side of Sydney Harbour (Port Jackson), from South Head to around Petersham, in Sydney, New South Wales, Australia

facts.text: Descendants of the Eora still live in Sydney today and proudly use the name Eora.
The City of Sydney formally acknowledges the Gadigal of the Eora Nation as the traditional custodians of the place now called Sydney.

nations.name: Larrakia
nations.lands: The Darwin region, from Cox Peninsula in the west to Gunn Point in the north, Northern Territory, Australia

facts.text: Larrakia Nation Aboriginal Corporation, set up in 1997, runs about 40 programs in Darwin, including the Larrakia Land and Sea Rangers.
Larrakia are the traditional owners of the Darwin region, with country reaching from Cox Peninsula in the west up to Gunn Point in the north.

nations.name: Marshallese
nations.lands: the atolls and islands of the Republic of the Marshall Islands, including Majuro

facts.text: Waan Aelõñ in Majel, Canoes of the Marshall Islands, is a Majuro program that trains young Marshallese women and men in skills for a sustainable future.

source.title: Canoes of the Marshall Islands, Waan Aelõñ in Majel

facts.text: In the Waan Aelõñ in Majel program, stick charts are still key tools for training new navigators in Marshallese wayfinding.

source.title: Canoes of the Marshall Islands, Waan Aelõñ in Majel

nations.name: Kaurna
nations.lands: The Adelaide Plains of South Australia, from around Crystal Brook in the north, bounded by the Mount Lofty Ranges to the east, Australia

facts.text: In March 2018 Kaurna people were recognised as native title holders around Adelaide, the first positive native title determination over a capital city area.

source.title: Native Title Recognition For Kaurna People Over Adelaide Area

facts.text: Requests for Kaurna names and translations all go through Kaurna Warra Karrpanthi, an Aboriginal corporation.

source.title: Aboriginal people of South Australia: Kaurna

nations.name: Torres Strait Islanders
nations.lands: the islands of the Torres Strait between Cape York and Papua New Guinea, in Queensland, Australia, and the Northern Peninsula Area

facts.text: The Torres Strait Regional Authority, an Australian Government body set up on 1 July 1994, counts recognising and maintaining Torres Strait Islander Ailan Kastom among its functions.
Kala Lagaw Ya is the traditional language of the western and central Torres Strait islands, and Meriam Mir is the language of the eastern islands.

nations.name: Noongar
nations.lands: The south-west of Western Australia, including the Perth region, Australia

facts.text: Western Australia's settlement recognises the Noongar people as the traditional owners of the South-West, with about A$1.3 billion in land and other benefits.

source.title: All six South West Native Title Settlement Agreements registered

facts.text: The South West Native Title Settlement covers about 200,000 square kilometres and affects an estimated 40,000 Noongar people.

source.title: South West Aboriginal Land and Sea Council
source.publisher: South West Aboriginal Land and Sea Council

nations.name: Yolŋu
nations.lands: North-east Arnhem Land, including the Gove Peninsula, Northern Territory, Australia

facts.text: Yolŋu elders founded Dhimurru Aboriginal Corporation to manage their land on the Gove Peninsula and the visitors who come to it.

source.title: Only Yolŋu make decisions for this land
source.publisher: Office of the Registrar of Indigenous Corporations (Australian Government)

facts.text: The name Dhimurru means east wind, the wind that carries the monsoon rains and brings new life to the land.

source.title: Only Yolŋu make decisions for this land
source.publisher: Office of the Registrar of Indigenous Corporations (Australian Government)

nations.name: Waikato-Tainui
nations.lands: The Waikato region of the North Island, Aotearoa New Zealand

facts.text: Waikato-Tainui describes itself as a growing tribe of over 90,000 people, voyagers and pioneers like their ancestors.

source.title: Ko Waikato te iwi, ko Tainui te waka

facts.text: Waikato-Tainui celebrate their identity as people of the Tainui waka and as protectors of the Kiingitanga movement.

source.title: Ko Waikato te iwi, ko Tainui te waka

nations.name: Niueans
nations.lands: the island of Niue in the South Pacific, with villages such as Alofi, Mutalau and Toi

facts.text: Fale Tāoga Niue, home of the Niue National Museum, opened on 19 October 2018, the anniversary of the Niue Constitution Celebrations.
Niue's Vagahau Niue Act 2012 recognises Vagahau Niue as the official language of Niue and created the Niue Language Commission to protect it.

source.title: Vagahau Niue Act 2012
source.publisher: Université Laval, CEFAN: L'aménagement linguistique dans le monde

nations.name: Samoans
nations.lands: the Independent State of Samoa, on Upolu, Savai'i and nearby islands

facts.text: Women and master weavers have formed fine mat committees in their villages, and more young women, and some men, now weave the 'ie Samoa.

source.title: 'Ie Samoa, fine mat and its cultural value

facts.text: Samoa's 2021 census counted 16,082 people aged 21 and over who hold a matai, or chiefly, title, including 1,444 women.

source.title: Samoa Population and Housing Census 2021 Fact Sheet (Final Results, October 2022)

nations.name: Rotumans
nations.lands: the island of Rotuma and its islets, about 500 km north of Fiji's main islands, and communities across Fiji

facts.text: Rotuma is divided into seven districts, each led by a district chief, the gagaj 'es itu'u, with village groups called ho'aga under their own chiefs.

source.title: Hierarchy (Kato'aga: Rotuman Ceremonies)
source.publisher: The Rotuma Website, University of Hawai'i

facts.text: In 2023 Fiji's President said some 2,000 Rotumans live on Rotuma, with more than 10,000 living elsewhere in Fiji.

source.title: His Excellency Ratu Wiliame Maivalili Katonivere's Speech at Rotuma Day 2023

nations.name: Kanak
nations.lands: New Caledonia, including Grande Terre and the Loyalty Islands

facts.text: Since 2016 every pupil in New Caledonia must be taught the fundamentals of Kanak culture, and every school must offer teaching in Kanak languages.

source.title: Organisation coutumière kanak
source.publisher: Institut de la statistique et des études économiques Nouvelle-Calédonie (ISEE)

facts.text: Kanak society is organised by custom: clans join into tribes within customary districts, which are grouped into eight customary areas.

source.title: Organisation coutumière kanak
source.publisher: Institut de la statistique et des études économiques Nouvelle-Calédonie (ISEE)

nations.name: Whanganui Iwi
nations.lands: The Whanganui River, from the mountains to the sea, North Island, Aotearoa New Zealand

facts.text: Ngā Tāngata Tiaki o Whanganui, the iwi river trust, was established in August 2014 with the signing of Ruruku Whakatupua.

source.title: Home | Ngā Tāngata Tiaki o Whanganui

facts.text: Since 2017, New Zealand law has recognised the Whanganui River, Te Awa Tupua, as a legal person, with a guardian office that acts as its human face.

source.title: The Whanganui River (Te Awa Tupua)
source.publisher: OsloMet (Oslo Metropolitan University), River Rights project

nations.name: Ngāi Tahu
nations.lands: Te Waipounamu (the South Island), Aotearoa New Zealand

facts.text: There are 18 Papatipu Rūnanga, local Ngāi Tahu councils, spread throughout Te Waipounamu, the South Island.

source.title: Ngāi Tahu | Te Rūnanga o Ngāi Tahu

facts.text: Ngāi Tahu means people of Tahu, and whakapapa, the ancestral link, binds all Ngāi Tahu whānau.

source.title: Ngāi Tahu | Te Rūnanga o Ngāi Tahu

nations.name: I-Kiribati
nations.lands: the Republic of Kiribati in the central Pacific, across the Gilbert, Phoenix and Line Islands

facts.text: In Kiribati the mwaneaba, the traditional meeting house, is where village decisions are made by the unimwane, the senior men, whose seating shows their standing.

source.title: Te Mwaneaba ni Kiribati: The Traditional Meeting House of Kiribati
source.publisher: Shima: The International Journal of Research into Island Cultures

facts.text: In 2010 the Phoenix Islands Protected Area, about 408,250 square kilometres of ocean and islands, became the first World Heritage site in Kiribati.

nations.name: Ngāti Whātua Ōrākei
nations.lands: Central Tāmaki Makaurau (Auckland), Aotearoa New Zealand

facts.text: Ngāti Whātua Ōrākei's shared affairs are looked after by their Trust and two subsidiaries: Whai Māia, the social arm, and Whai Rawa, the commercial arm.
Ngāti Whātua Ōrākei are the tangata whenua, the people of the land, of Te Kahu Tōpuni o Tuperiri in central Tāmaki Makaurau (Auckland).

nations.name: Refaluwasch
nations.lands: Saipan and other islands of the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands, a United States commonwealth in the western Pacific

facts.text: In December 2020 the Matawal Wóól Display Hall opened with photos and crafts made by students of the Tepengi Kkosch Refaluwasch culture program.

source.title: Carolinian Affairs Office 2021 Citizen Centric Report

facts.text: The Carolinian Affairs Office, created by the CNMI Constitution, advises the governor and works to protect and preserve the culture and traditions of Indigenous Carolinians.

source.title: Carolinian Affairs Office 2020 Citizen Centric Report

nations.name: Pohnpeians
nations.lands: Pohnpei State in the Federated States of Micronesia, on Pohnpei island and its outlying atolls

facts.text: Nan Madol, a World Heritage site since 2016, is traditionally owned and managed under the Nahnmwarki system, a chiefly institution that continues in Pohnpei today.

source.title: Nan Madol: Ceremonial Centre of Eastern Micronesia

facts.text: Pohnpei State's constitution protects the customs and traditions of Pohnpei's traditional kingdoms alongside its elected government.

source.title: Pohnpei
source.publisher: Legal Information System of the Federated States of Micronesia

nations.name: Hla'alua
nations.lands: Taoyuan and Namaxia districts, Kaohsiung City, Taiwan

facts.text: In 2014 the Hla'alua were officially recognized as a distinct people, becoming the 15th Indigenous people listed in Taiwan.
The Hla'alua are formed by four communities, Paiciana, Vilanganʉ, Talicia and Hlihlara, in Kaohsiung City.

nations.name: Tsou
nations.lands: Alishan Township in Chiayi County, plus Nantou and Kaohsiung, Taiwan

facts.text: The Tsou homeland centres on Alishan Township in Chiayi County, southwest of Yushan in central Taiwan.
The Tsou population was 6,702 in January 2020.

nations.name: Mentawai
nations.lands: The Mentawai Islands, including Siberut, off West Sumatra, Indonesia

facts.text: On Siberut, a UNESCO biosphere reserve since 1981, Mentawai communities use the forest with care, guided by traditional knowledge.

source.title: Siberut Biosphere Reserve, Indonesia
source.publisher: UNESCO Man and the Biosphere Programme

facts.text: Siberut, home to many Mentawai communities, is the largest of the four Mentawai Islands west of Sumatra.

source.title: Siberut Biosphere Reserve, Indonesia
source.publisher: UNESCO Man and the Biosphere Programme

nations.name: Khasi
nations.lands: Khasi Hills of Meghalaya, India, and nearby Bangladesh

facts.text: The Khasi Hills Autonomous District Council has a wing that oversees the Elakas, the traditional Khasi states.

source.title: General Administration Department and Elaka Administration

facts.text: Apart from Shillong's municipality and cantonment, all of Meghalaya is governed under the Sixth Schedule, the only northeast state where this is so.

nations.name: Ibaloi
nations.lands: Southern Benguet and the Baguio area in northern Luzon, Philippines

facts.text: The Ibaloi are one of the three major ethnolinguistic groups of Benguet province, with the Kankanaey and Kalanguya.
Benguet's official provincial fruit is a native blueberry whose Ibaloi name is ayosip.

nations.name: Tripura
nations.lands: Chittagong Hill Tracts and other districts of Bangladesh, and the state of Tripura, India

facts.text: In Bangladesh, Tripura communities live in the Chittagong Hill Tracts and in districts such as Comilla, Chandpur, Moulvibazar and Dhaka.

nations.name: Saisiyat
nations.lands: Hsinchu and Miaoli counties in northwestern Taiwan

facts.text: The Saisiyat live in northwestern Taiwan, in Hsinchu County and Miaoli County on either side of Ngangihaw mountain.
The Saisiyat population was 6,730 in January 2020.

nations.name: Truku
nations.lands: Xiulin, Wanrong and Zhuoxi townships in Hualien County, Taiwan

facts.text: The Truku were officially recognized as one of Taiwan's Indigenous peoples in 2004.
About 32,333 Truku people were counted in January 2020, mostly in Hualien County.

nations.name: Kalasha
nations.lands: The Kalasha valleys of Bamburet, Birir and Rumbur in the Hindu Kush, Chitral, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan

facts.text: Kalasha families use Suri Jagek to choose the right time to sow seeds and care for livestock, and to anticipate natural hazards.
Suri Jagek, meaning observing the sun, is the Kalasha system of reading the sun, moon, stars and shadows; UNESCO listed it for urgent safeguarding in 2018.

nations.name: Sakizaya
nations.lands: Hualien Plain, the East Rift Valley and coast, Taiwan

facts.text: Through a cultural revival led by the community itself, the Sakizaya were recognized as one of Taiwan's Indigenous peoples in 2007.
The Sakizaya population was about 985 in January 2020.

nations.name: Yakthung
nations.lands: Limbuwan in the eastern hills of Nepal, including Taplejung, Panchthar, Terhathum and Ilam, plus Jhapa, Morang and Sunsari, with communities in Sikkim and Darjeeling, India

facts.text: In Nepal's 2021 census, 84.5 percent of Yakthung people reported Limbu as their mother tongue, a language with its own script, Sirijanga.

source.title: लिम्बु (Limbu)
source.publisher: National Foundation for Development of Indigenous Nationalities, Nepal

facts.text: In 2021 Nepal's Language Commission recommended Limbu, alongside Maithili, as an official language of Province 1 in eastern Nepal.

source.title: Language Commission recommends province-wise official languages before government

nations.name: Tharu
nations.lands: The Terai plains of southern Nepal, and neighbouring India

facts.text: The Tharu are on the Nepal government's official list of Adivasi Janajati, or Indigenous nationalities.

source.title: Adivasi Janajati list
source.publisher: National Foundation for Development of Indigenous Nationalities, Nepal

nations.name: Mizo
nations.lands: Mizoram, northeast India

facts.text: Mizoram became a full state of India on 20 February 1987; its Legislative Assembly first met on 10 May 1972.
Historically, every Mizo village had its own chief, who was assisted by a council of elders.

nations.name: Thao
nations.lands: Ita Thao Village by Sun Moon Lake and Dapinglin, Nantou County, Taiwan

facts.text: Thao people live mainly in Ita Thao Village in Yuchi Township and in Dapinglin, Shuili Township, both in Nantou County. They numbered about 817 in January 2020.
Thao oral history tells of ancestors who followed a white deer to Sun Moon Lake and found a fertile place full of fish.

nations.name: Pinuyumayan
nations.lands: Taitung City and Beinan Township on the Taitung Plain, Taiwan

facts.text: Taitung City and Beinan Township on the Taitung Plain are the heart of Pinuyumayan life today.
About 14,517 Pinuyumayan people were counted in January 2020, and many have moved from eastern Taiwan to cities, where they are active in many fields.

nations.name: Santal
nations.lands: Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha and nearby states of India, northwest Bangladesh, and Nepal

facts.text: Odisha counted 894,764 Santal people in the 2011 census, most living in settled villages of 50 to 100 households.

source.title: Odisha State Tribal Museum: Santal
source.publisher: Odisha State Tribal Museum (SCSTRTI, Government of Odisha)

facts.text: Santal homes in Odisha are decorated with wall paintings of animals, people and flowers.

source.title: Odisha State Tribal Museum: Santal
source.publisher: Odisha State Tribal Museum (SCSTRTI, Government of Odisha)

nations.name: Munda
nations.lands: Jharkhand, Odisha, West Bengal, Chhattisgarh and Bihar in India, with communities in Bangladesh

facts.text: Mundari has its own script, known in the community as Mundari Bani; a version reformed in 2008 by Munda community bodies is in the Unicode Standard.

source.title: Chapter 13, South and Central Asia-II (The Unicode Standard, Version 18.0)

facts.text: Munda call their dance durang and their song susun, and both women and men dance at social events and seasonal festivals.

source.title: Munda
source.publisher: Dr. Ramdayal Munda Tribal Welfare Research Institute, Jharkhand

nations.name: Atayal
nations.lands: Mountain areas of northern and central Taiwan, across New Taipei, Taoyuan, Hsinchu, Miaoli, Taichung, Nantou and Yilan

facts.text: In the Atayal language, the word Atayal means people, real people, or kinspeople.
The Atayal live across the mountains of northern and central Taiwan, the widest spread of any Indigenous people on the island.

nations.name: Kanakanavu
nations.lands: Namaxia District, Kaohsiung City, Taiwan

facts.text: On June 26, 2014, Taiwan's government recognized the Kanakanavu as an independent people, the 16th on the official list.
Some Kanakanavu people understand their name as people living in a forest of Taiwan giant bamboo.

nations.name: Mru
nations.lands: Bandarban district in the Chittagong Hill Tracts of Bangladesh, and nearby areas of Myanmar

facts.text: The Mru alphabet, invented in the 1980s and unrelated to any other script, is encoded in the Unicode Standard with its own digits.

source.title: Chapter 13, South and Central Asia-II (The Unicode Standard, Version 18.0)

facts.text: School textbooks up to class three have been published in the Mru language and alphabet.

nations.name: Kavalan
nations.lands: Yilan and the Hualien and Taitung coasts, Taiwan

facts.text: After a name rectification movement, the Kavalan were officially recognized as one of Taiwan's Indigenous peoples in 2002.
The Kavalan population was about 1,492 in January 2020.

nations.name: Kadazandusun
nations.lands: Sabah, Malaysia

facts.text: The Kadazan Dusun Cultural Association, founded in 1966, represents 48 Indigenous ethnic communities of Sabah.
KDCA works on preserving, standardizing and developing the Kadazandusun language with its many dialects.

nations.name: Osage Nation
nations.lands: Osage Nation Reservation, northeastern Oklahoma, United States; headquarters in Pawhuska

facts.text: The Osage Minerals Council, an elected body of eight members, is part of the Osage Nation's government.
Since 2006 the Osage Nation has governed itself under a constitution with separate executive, legislative and judicial branches.

nations.name: Standing Rock Sioux Tribe
nations.lands: Standing Rock Reservation, across North Dakota and South Dakota, United States

facts.text: Today Yanktonai Dakota communities live mostly on the North Dakota side of Standing Rock, and Lakota communities mostly on the South Dakota side.
The Standing Rock Tribal Council has a Chairman, Vice-Chairman, Secretary and 14 council members, all elected by tribal members for four-year terms.

source.title: Standing Rock Sioux Tribe | Indian Affairs Commission, North Dakota

nations.name: Pawnee Nation of Oklahoma
nations.lands: Pawnee, Oklahoma, United States; ancestral homeland on the central Plains

facts.text: The Pawnee Business Council is the supreme governing body of the Pawnee Nation, acting within the nation's Constitution and federal law.
The Pawnee Nation is made up of four bands: the Čawî’ (Grand), Kitkahaki (Republican), Pitahawirata (Tappage) and Skidi (Wolf).

source.title: Pawnee History | Pawnee Nation of Oklahoma

nations.name: Bad River Band of Lake Superior Chippewa
nations.lands: Along Lake Superior and Chequamegon Bay in northern Wisconsin.

facts.text: Its Water Resources page dates the Band's adoption of Water Quality Standards to July 6, 2011.

source.title: Water Resources
source.publisher: Bad River Band of Lake Superior Chippewa

facts.text: The Band's Energy page dates completion and commissioning of its microgrids to May 2021, following emergency-planning changes after the 2016 flood.

source.title: Energy
source.publisher: Bad River Band of Lake Superior Chippewa

nations.name: Fort Sill Apache Tribe
nations.lands: Apache and Fletcher, Oklahoma; reservation land in New Mexico, United States

facts.text: The Fort Sill Apache Tribe comprises descendants of Chiricahua and Warm Springs Apaches displaced from the Southwest and northern Mexico.
The General Council, made up of adult tribal members, elects the Business Committee and approves the tribal operations budget.

nations.name: Oneida Nation
also: Oneida Tribe of Indians of Wisconsin
nations.lands: Oneida Reservation, Brown and Outagamie counties, northeast Wisconsin, United States

facts.text: The Oneida Nation is governed by an elected Business Committee of nine members, which makes decisions by majority rule.

source.title: Oneida Nation | Department of Public Instruction

facts.text: The Oneida Reservation lies in Brown and Outagamie counties in northeast Wisconsin.

source.title: Oneida Nation | Department of Public Instruction

nations.name: Ponca Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma
nations.lands: Oklahoma; the Tribe publishes its offices in Ponca City

facts.text: The Tribe lists preparing an annual funding agreement for Tribal Council review and approval among its self-governance office's duties.

source.title: Self-Governance
source.publisher: Ponca Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma

facts.text: The Tribe describes preservation work that includes Section 106 reviews and consultation with federal, Tribal, state and local agencies.

source.title: Historic Preservation
source.publisher: Ponca Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma

nations.name: Citizen Potawatomi Nation
nations.lands: Headquartered in Shawnee, Oklahoma, United States, with citizens around the world

facts.text: In July 2026 the Citizen Potawatomi Nation signed the articles of confederation for the Potawatomi Confederacy.
The Citizen Potawatomi Nation Constitution dates from 1938 and was amended in 1985 and again in 2007.

nations.name: Kaw Nation
nations.lands: Oklahoma, with historical homelands in Kansas and the Great Plains

facts.text: The Nation's history distinguishes a Tribal Council from a General Council composed of enrolled adult citizens.
The Nation's language page lists online learning and a basic Kanza course. Listed materials remain under the publisher's access and use conditions.

nations.name: Sisseton Wahpeton Oyate
nations.lands: Lake Traverse Reservation, northeastern South Dakota and southeastern North Dakota, United States

facts.text: The Lake Traverse Reservation reaches across seven counties, five in South Dakota and two in North Dakota.
The Oyate counts more than 14,000 tribal members, living across the United States and serving abroad in the Armed Forces.

nations.name: Forest County Potawatomi
nations.lands: Forest County, northern Wisconsin, United States

facts.text: The Forest County Potawatomi Language and Culture Department works to keep the Bodwéwadmi language and traditions alive, with classes during the school year.
The Forest County Potawatomi Cultural Center, Library and Museum provides an important link to the community's past.

nations.name: Red Lake Nation
also: Red Lake Band of Chippewa Indians
nations.lands: Red Lake Reservation, northern Minnesota, United States

facts.text: The Red Lake tribal government holds full sovereignty over its reservation, subject only to the federal government.

source.title: Red Lake Nation - Home of the Red Lake Band of Chippewa Indians

facts.text: English is a second language for many Red Lake members who are middle-aged and older, including some on the Tribal Council, and many others speak or understand Ojibwe.

nations.name: Kiowa Tribe
nations.lands: Southwestern Oklahoma, United States

facts.text: The Kiowa Tribe commits to protecting its sovereignty and to preserving and advocating for Kiowa culture and language.

source.title: Kiowa Tribe - Tribe, Native American, Native, Tribe

facts.text: The Kiowa Language Department runs a credentialed teacher training program to prepare new Kiowa language teachers.

pronounce.text: Gáuigú, as in Gáuigú bà dàu, We are Kiowa: Gkawy-goo
pronounce.publisher: Kiowa Tribe, on its own site

nations.name: Blackfeet Nation
nations.lands: Blackfeet Reservation, northwestern Montana, bordering Canada and Glacier National Park, United States

facts.text: The Nation’s water chronology dates establishment of a Water Department by resolution to 2018.
The Nation’s compact page records an April 20, 2017 vote by Tribal members in favor of the Blackfeet Water Compact and Settlement Act.

nations.name: Little Traverse Bay Bands of Odawa Indians
nations.lands: Northern Lower Peninsula of Michigan, United States

facts.text: The tribe is governed by a nine-member Tribal Council whose members serve staggered terms.

source.title: Home - LTBB Official Website
source.publisher: Little Traverse Bay Bands of Odawa Indians

facts.text: The tribe's mission celebrates that its people still have and speak their own language, Anishinaabemowin.

source.title: Home - LTBB Official Website
source.publisher: Little Traverse Bay Bands of Odawa Indians

nations.name: Menominee Indian Tribe of Wisconsin
nations.lands: Menominee Reservation, northeastern Wisconsin, United States

facts.text: The Menominee Tribal Legislature has nine members.
The Menominee Reservation covers about 235,524 acres in Wisconsin and holds the largest single tract of virgin timberland in the state.

nations.name: Otoe-Missouria Tribe
nations.lands: Red Rock, Oklahoma; historical homelands include Nebraska and the lower Missouri River valley

facts.text: The Tribe's government page describes a seven-member Tribal Council elected by qualified Tribal voters using a secret ballot.
The Tribe's preservation page dates National Park Service recognition of its Tribal Historic Preservation Office to spring 2016.

nations.name: Fort Peck Assiniboine and Sioux Tribes
nations.lands: Fort Peck Reservation, northeastern Montana, United States; headquarters in Poplar

facts.text: Members of the Fort Peck Tribal Executive Board, except the secretary-accountant, are elected at-large every two years.

source.title: Fort Peck Assiniboine and Sioux Tribes
source.publisher: Montana Governor's Office of Indian Affairs

facts.text: The Fort Peck Reservation in northeastern Montana includes more than two million acres of land.

source.title: Fort Peck Assiniboine and Sioux Tribes
source.publisher: Montana Governor's Office of Indian Affairs

nations.name: Prairie Band Potawatomi Nation
nations.lands: Reservation near Mayetta, northeastern Kansas, United States

facts.text: The Nation has offered Potawatomi language classes since 2007 as part of its work to revitalize the language and culture.

source.title: Prairie Band Potawatomi Language Revitalization Efforts

facts.text: The Prairie Band Potawatomi Nation says its Kansas reservation is unchanged from what the Treaty of 1846 established.

source.title: Prairie Band Potawatomi Tribal History: Origins, Separation, and Stewardship

nations.name: Ho-Chunk Nation
nations.lands: Wisconsin, United States, on lands in many places rather than one reservation; traditional lands also reach Minnesota, Iowa, Missouri and Illinois

facts.text: The Ho-Chunk Nation has four branches of government, with a legislature of 13 members elected from four districts.
Alongside its constitutional government, the Ho-Chunk Nation keeps a traditional system of leadership based on chiefs and clans.

nations.name: Sicangu Lakota Oyate
nations.lands: Rosebud Reservation, South Dakota, United States

facts.text: The tribe's history page says the Lakota number about 70,000 today, and that about a third of them still speak their ancestral language.
The Rosebud Reservation takes in 20 communities, and the tribal headquarters is in the community of Rosebud, South Dakota.

nations.name: Seminole Nation of Oklahoma
also: The Great Seminole Nation of Oklahoma
nations.lands: Wewoka and Seminole County, Oklahoma, United States; earlier homelands in Florida

facts.text: The Seminole Nation of Oklahoma is made up of fourteen bands, and its General Council seats two representatives from each band rather than from districts.

source.title: The Great Seminole Nation of Oklahoma: Written Testimony to the Senate Committee on Indian Affairs
source.publisher: Seminole Nation of Oklahoma, via U.S. Senate Committee on Indian Affairs

facts.text: The Seminole Nation Language Program works to maintain, revitalize and carry forward the language and traditional ways of the Seminole people.

nations.name: Rappahannock Indian Tribe
nations.lands: the lower Rappahannock and Mattaponi river watersheds in Virginia, as described by the Tribe's environmental department

facts.text: The Tribe's environmental department says it coordinates the Return to the River youth program.

source.title: Department Of Environmental Services | Rappahannock Indian Tribe

facts.text: The Tribe dates its incorporation to 1921 as part of efforts to strengthen its government and seek recognition.

nations.name: United Cherokee AniYunWiYa Nation
nations.lands: Guntersville, Alabama

facts.text: A January 2020 post describes a Word of the Month practice series, with a new calendar of practice planned for February.
In January 2020, the Nation announced a plan to highlight enrolled citizens' crafted items in its public posts.

source.title: Attention: United Cherokee AniYunWiYa Nation Artisans - UCAN

nations.name: Saint Regis Mohawk Tribe
nations.lands: Akwesasne, on the St. Lawrence River in northern New York, United States; the wider Akwesasne community extends into Canada

facts.text: The Saint Regis Mohawk Tribal Council is made up of three Chiefs, three Sub-Chiefs and a Tribal Clerk, with elections scheduled each year and set terms of office.

source.title: History of Tribal Government | SRMT - NSN

facts.text: The Tribe describes its original homeland as northeastern New York State, reaching into southern Canada and Vermont.

source.title: History of Tribal Government | SRMT - NSN

nations.name: Coharie Tribe
nations.lands: Harnett and Sampson Counties in southeastern North Carolina, where the Tribe locates its present community

facts.text: The Tribe's government page describes the Coharie Intra-Tribal Council as representing Harnett and Sampson Counties.
The Tribe's history locates the present Coharie population in North Carolina's Harnett and Sampson Counties.

nations.name: Seneca Nation
nations.lands: Allegany, Cattaraugus and Oil Spring territories in Western New York, United States

facts.text: The Seneca Nation governs itself under a constitution established in 1848, with a 16-member Tribal Council drawn equally from the Cattaraugus and Allegany territories.

source.title: Seneca Nation of Indians - Official Website

facts.text: The Seneca Nation runs a language immersion program so students can hold conversations in Onöndowa’ga:’ Gawë:nö’, the Seneca language, alongside classes and online learning.

nations.name: Cherokee Nation
nations.lands: Tahlequah and a 14-county reservation area in Oklahoma, United States; original homelands in the Southeast

facts.text: Cherokee Nation governs through legislative, executive and judicial branches and serves people across a 14-county reservation area.
Written Cherokee uses a syllabary, not an alphabet, with 85 distinct characters; Cherokee Nation teaches it through an immersion school and a master-apprentice program.

nations.name: Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians
nations.lands: The Qualla Boundary in western North Carolina, United States, beside the Great Smoky Mountains

facts.text: As a sovereign nation, the Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians makes its own laws, holds its own elections and runs its own government and institutions.

source.title: Home - Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians

facts.text: The Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians makes its home on the 56,000-acre Qualla Boundary, next to Great Smoky Mountains National Park.

source.title: NC Tribal Communities | NC DOA
source.publisher: North Carolina Department of Administration, Commission of Indian Affairs

nations.name: Seminole Tribe of Florida
nations.lands: Big Cypress, Brighton, Fort Pierce, Hollywood, Immokalee and Tampa reservations in Florida, United States

facts.text: The Tribal Council, with a Chairman, a Vice-Chairman and representatives from each reservation, is the chief governing body of the Seminole Tribe of Florida.
Adding the Tampa and Immokalee reservations brought the Seminole Tribe of Florida's federal trust lands to more than 90,000 acres.

nations.name: Southeastern Mvskoke Nation
nations.lands: Near Troy in Alabama; its history describes organization around Pike and Coffee Counties.

Its introduction locates the Nation near Troy in Alabama.

nations.name: Delaware Tribe of Indians
nations.lands: Bartlesville, Oklahoma, United States; homelands along the Delaware River

facts.text: The Delaware Tribe of Indians is a federally recognized tribe of the Lenape people, headquartered in Bartlesville, Oklahoma.
The Tribe's online Lenape Talking Dictionary holds about 15,380 words, along with recorded stories and songs, and is still growing.

source.title: Language Revitalization - Delaware Tribe of Indians

pronounce.publisher: Delaware Tribe of Indians, on its own site

nations.name: Coushatta Tribe of Louisiana
nations.lands: Southwest Louisiana; the Tribe describes a community centered in Allen Parish

The Tribe describes a five-member elected council: four council members and a chairman.

nations.name: Passamaquoddy (Peskotomuhkati)
nations.lands: Sipayik (Pleasant Point) and Motahkomikuk (Indian Township) in Maine, United States, and a community in New Brunswick, Canada

facts.text: Over 3,000 Passamaquoddy citizens belong to three self-governing communities, two in Maine and one in New Brunswick, linked by political, cultural and kinship ties.
The Maliseet-Passamaquoddy Dictionary has more than 19,000 entries, and many older tribal members still speak the language fluently.

nations.name: MOWA Band of Choctaw Indians
nations.lands: Mobile and Washington Counties in southwestern Alabama, near the Mobile and Tombigbee Rivers

Its history dates an effort to obtain federal aid for Alabama Choctaw schools to 1934.

source.title: Social Barriers - MOWA Band of Choctaw Indians

nations.name: Mississippi Band of Choctaw Indians
nations.lands: Choctaw communities in east-central Mississippi, United States

facts.text: In 1945 the Mississippi Band of Choctaw Indians ratified a Constitution that authorized the Tribe's separation from the state of Mississippi.

source.title: About Us - Mississippi Band of Choctaw Indians

facts.text: The Mississippi Band of Choctaw Indians has more than 11,000 tribal members.

source.title: Home Page - Mississippi Band of Choctaw Indians

nations.name: Choctaw Nation of Oklahoma
nations.lands: Durant and a reservation of eight whole and five partial counties in southeastern Oklahoma, United States; original homelands in present-day Mississippi

facts.text: Chahta Anumpa Aiikhvna, the School of Choctaw Language, offers classes for every skill level plus a Speak Choctaw app.
The Choctaw Nation reservation covers 10,864 square miles in southeastern Oklahoma, taking in eight whole counties and parts of five more.

nations.name: Cheroenhaka (Nottoway) Indian Tribe
nations.lands: Southampton County, Virginia, United States

facts.text: Cheroenhaka (Nottoway) Indian Tribe is based in Southampton County, Virginia.
The Tribe's language page publishes a vocabulary drawn from materials dating to March 4, 1820.

nations.lands: East Texas; the Tribe describes its reservation in the Big Thicket

nations.name: Shinnecock Indian Nation
nations.lands: In and around the Town of Southampton on the eastern end of Long Island, New York, United States

facts.text: On October 1, 2010, the Shinnecock Indian Nation was formally recognized by the United States as the 565th federally recognized tribe.
The Shinnecock Indian Nation has over 1,589 enrolled tribal members.

nations.name: Nottoway Indian Tribe of Virginia
nations.lands: southeastern Virginia along the Nottoway River; the Tribe's Community House & Interpretive Center is in Capron

facts.text: The Tribe's history describes the Nottoway as Iroquoian speakers of southeastern Virginia.

source.title: Tribal History - Nottoway Indian Tribe of Virginia

facts.text: The Tribe says its Community House & Interpretive Center formally opened in Capron on May 5, 2012.

source.title: Community House & Interpretive Center - Nottoway Indian Tribe of Virginia

nations.name: Lumbee Tribe of North Carolina
nations.lands: Along the Lumbee River in Robeson, Hoke, Cumberland and Scotland counties, North Carolina, United States, centered on Pembroke

facts.text: The Lumbee Tribe became fully federally recognized by the United States on December 18, 2025.
The Lumbee Tribe describes its people, the People of the Dark Water, as entrepreneurial and strongly focused on education.

nations.name: Muskeg Lake Cree Nation
nations.lands: Treaty 6 territory in central Saskatchewan, Canada, with urban reserve land in Saskatoon

facts.text: Muskeg Lake Cree Nation planned a gathering for August 20 to 23, 2026 to mark 150 years since Treaty 6 was signed.

source.title: Muskeg Lake Cree Nation, Band No. 102

facts.text: In 1988 Muskeg Lake Cree Nation created Asimakeniseekan Askiy in Saskatoon, the first commercial urban reserve in Canada.

nations.name: Gitxsan
nations.lands: The Laxyip along the upper Skeena River and its tributaries in northern British Columbia, Canada

facts.text: Gitxsan society is matriarchal, with four clans made up of independent Houses (Huwilp), each led by a Wii Simoogit, or high chief.
Gitxsanimaax, the traditional Gitxsan language, has two dialects: Giigeenix, spoken up river, and Gyeets, spoken down river.

nations.name: Piikani Nation
nations.lands: Around Brocket in southern Alberta, Canada, near the Old Man River; part of the Blackfoot Confederacy

facts.text: Piikani stories, ceremonies and songs describe an ancestral territory reaching north to the North Saskatchewan River and west into the Rocky Mountains.
The international border divides the Piikani into the Aapatohsipiikani, or North Piikani, in Canada and the Amsskapipiikani, or South Piikani, in the United States.

nations.name: Atikamekw
nations.lands: Nitaskinan in central Quebec, Canada, with the communities of Manawan, Wemotaci and Opitciwan

facts.text: The Atikamekw language, like other Algonquin and Anishinaabe languages, is rich in imagery and names things by how they truly are.
Young people aged 0 to 35 make up about 65 percent of the Atikamekw population today.

nations.name: Innu
nations.lands: Nitassinan: Labrador (Newfoundland and Labrador) and eastern Quebec, Canada

facts.text: In 2008 the Innu Nation and Newfoundland and Labrador signed the Tshash Petapen, or New Dawn, Agreement.

source.title: Innu Nation of Labrador
source.publisher: Government of Newfoundland and Labrador, Indigenous Affairs and Reconciliation

facts.text: The Innu Nation land claim, accepted for negotiation in 1978, covers about 70 percent of Labrador.

source.title: Innu Nation of Labrador
source.publisher: Government of Newfoundland and Labrador, Indigenous Affairs and Reconciliation

nations.name: Six Nations of the Grand River
nations.lands: Along the Grand River in southern Ontario, Canada

facts.text: It is the only First Nation community home to all six Haudenosaunee nations: Mohawk, Cayuga, Onondaga, Oneida, Seneca and Tuscarora.

source.title: Who We Are
source.publisher: Six Nations of the Grand River

facts.text: No First Nation in Canada has a larger population than Six Nations of the Grand River.

source.title: Who We Are
source.publisher: Six Nations of the Grand River

nations.name: Haíɫzaqv
nations.lands: The Central Coast of British Columbia, Canada, centred on Bella Bella (Wáglísla) on Campbell Island

facts.text: In 2025 Heiltsuk members ratified a written constitution, a milestone in self-governance.
Haíɫzaqv means 'to speak and act correctly', principles that guide Heiltsuk ancestral and present-day ways of life.

nations.name: Tłı̨chǫ
nations.lands: Between Great Slave Lake and Great Bear Lake in the Northwest Territories, Canada, around the communities of Behchokǫ̀, Whatì, Gamètì and Wekweètì
